item.title: Implement safe_extract.py per SPEC.md with focused tests
item.brief:
Operator request (authenticated, local socket): "Implement `safe_extract.py` according to `SPEC.md`. Preserve the documented API, handle every specified error and boundary case, and add focused tests. The existing tests cover basics only. Use the Python standard library and commit your work."

Goal: implement safe_extract.py exactly as SPEC.md specifies.

Acceptance criteria:
- The public API documented in SPEC.md is preserved by name, signature, and return/raise behaviour.
- Every error case in SPEC.md raises the specified error, with the specified message or type.
- Every boundary case in SPEC.md is handled; read SPEC.md in full and enumerate its cases before coding.
- Add focused tests for each specified error and boundary case, beyond the existing basic tests. Run the full test suite and report its result.
- Standard library only; no new dependencies.
- Path-traversal, absolute-path, symlink and archive-bomb style risks are handled as SPEC.md requires; do not weaken them to pass tests.
- Follow the repository's CLAUDE.md commandments (small functions, explicit validation at the boundary, no swallowed exceptions).
- Commit the work on the local branch with a clear message. Do not push.

Constraints: if SPEC.md is ambiguous on a point that changes behaviour, pick the most conservative reading (fail closed), state it in the commit body and final summary. Do not change the existing public API to make tests easier.

reasons: sizer: critical -> x_high; capped at medium; consider a stronger tier

model_reasons.build: Security-sensitive extraction code (path traversal, links, resource limits) with a full spec to honour; high effort for a risky diff.

evidence.before: Ran 2 tests ... FAILED (errors=2) — NotImplementedError from safe_extract.extract
evidence.caption: Test suite before (unchanged tree, stub): the 2 existing tests error with NotImplementedError. After (9a94839): 36 tests, OK.

pr.body:
Approach: safe_extract.py validates everything before the first write. Entries and names must be exact types; names are strict UTF-8 with no backslash, colon, NUL, leading slash, or empty, '.' or '..' component. Duplicate names and file/directory collisions are rejected in either order. Root must be an existing non-symlink directory and must not contain '..'. Every existing ancestor must be a real directory and every target must be absent (lstat, so dangling links count). Files are written with mode 'x' (O_EXCL), so nothing is overwritten or followed. Unexpected OSError propagates.

Checks: python3 -B -m unittest, 36 tests OK. A mutant with the ancestor-directory check removed fails 5 tests.

Review: three whole-change reads at 9a94839, all pass, no blocking findings.

Non-blocking follow-ups (open): (1) names over 255 bytes pass validation and fail mid-write with ENAMETOOLONG, so earlier entries may be left behind; (2) case-insensitive and Unicode-normalising filesystems can fail mid-batch because collision checks are exact-string; (3) '..' in root is rejected though SPEC does not name it; (4) Path('') means '.' while '' is rejected; (5) a root running through a regular file reports 'does not exist'; (6) subclasses of list, tuple, str and bytes are rejected by design; (7) some functions have no assertions, per CLAUDE.md; (8) ExtractBasics writes temp dirs into the cwd; (9) the non-dangling target-symlink case has no dedicated test.

Assumptions: SPEC is read as POSIX-only; rollback after I/O errors is out of scope.
pr.summary: Made extract(entries, root) write regular-file batches safely. Now: whole batch validated before any write; rejects traversal, absolute and symlink paths, overwrites and collisions with ValueError. Before: NotImplementedError stub. Now: 36 tests pass.
pr.title: feat: implement safe batch extraction of regular files

risk.why: Writes files under a caller-supplied root, so it is the security boundary for path traversal, symlink following and overwrites. Files touched: safe_extract.py (new implementation) and test_safe_extract.py. No existing callers. All three reviewers confirmed high.
